news.title: Journalist confirms Liverpool are ‘definitely looking at’ player who starred at the World Cup
news.lede: Liverpool’s interest in Gilberto Mora is very real, but the Reds are far from alone in the race for one of world football’s most exciting teenagers.The Club Tijuana attacking midfielder has attracted attention across Europe after a remarkable rise for both club and country.Mora starred for Mexico at the 2026 World Cup and is already playing senior football regularly despite not turning 18 until October 14. Liverpool clearly like what they see, although suggestions they are leading the chase appear premature.David Lynch confirms Liverpool are watching MoraSpeaking on Anfield Index’s Media Matters , Liverpool reporter David Lynch confirmed that Mora fits the type of young player the club are actively scouting.“. Yeah, and a lot of links to Liverpool.

news.title: Denise O'Sullivan's World Cup Admission Speaks Volumes As Ireland Edge Closer In Cork
news.lede: "Why would I be captain?!" Denise O'Sullivan is incredulous when asked if she could captain Ireland in her hometown of Cork on Tuesday night, but she would certainly be a popular choice among the Rebel faithful. Over 10,000 tickets have been sold for the second leg of Ireland's World Cup playoff semi-final against Kazakhstan, for which O'Sullivan and Katie McCabe will return to the side. Ireland's two key players missed Friday's first leg in Astana, not that you might have guessed from the stunningly comprehensive 8-0 win.

news.title: Ronaldo and other veterans still going strong ahead of 2026 FIFA World Cup
news.lede: The 2026 FIFA World Cup is expected to showcase the sport’s next generation of stars, but several players in their 40s are still competing at the highest international level. When the tournament kicks off across the United States, Canada and Mexico, these veteran names will not just be making up the numbers. From experienced goalkeepers to former Ballon d’Or winners, each is still expected to play an important role for their respective countries on football’s biggest stage. Perhaps surprisingly, Nagatomo was called up by Japan head coach Hajime Moriyasu despite his limited involvement with the national team in recent years.

news.title: Beyond Sponsorship: How Football’s Commercial Power Can Become a Force for Good
news.lede: Football crosses borders, creates communities and gives millions of people a shared language. That reach also gives the industry an opportunity to create value beyond the pitch. For the Homeless World Cup Foundation, commercial partnerships can play an important role in unlocking that potential. The aim is not simply to secure sponsorship, but to build relationships with organisations that can contribute their expertise, networks and people to help extend the impact of football.
